title: serving-runtime-weekly-update-kernel-kv-batching-2026-08-12
content:
Week: 2026-08-05 -> 2026-08-12
Owners: Ben (kernel), Aisha (kv cache), Chen (batching)

Summary / Highlights:
- Kernel: landed fused-attention microkernel v2 on Triton backend (PR 1987). Early internal benchmarks show 12-18% lower latencies for 2k-context LlaMA-like models at batch sizes >1. Still seeing nvcc differences across G5 vs A100.
- KV Cache: prototype sharded KV map implemented. Sharding reduces memcopy hotspots on multi-tenant hosts; p95 memcopy ops down ~40% in stress tests.
- Batching: adaptive continuous-batching (alpha) rolled out to staging for the hosted API. Observed 7% token-cost reduction and 10% p99 latency improvement for median traffic patterns.

Blockers / Risks:
- Kernel: fused-attention v2 regresses slightly on float16 under long-seq edgecases (repro on g5x with seq=4096). Root cause likely small numeric differences from reordered reductions. Need formal repro and unit test. (owner: Ben)
- KV cache: sharding introduces extra lookups for cold prefixes; spike in tail-latency during warmup. Need better prefetch heuristics. (owner: Aisha)
- Batching: alpha adaptive algo sometimes oversizes batches when traffic has short bursts, causing p50 latency spikes for low-latency routes. Need route-weighted constraints. (owner: Chen)

Kernel work (Ben)
- Done:
  - PR 1987 merged: fused-attention microkernel v2 (Triton + CUDA 12 optimized). Perf matrix added to repo.
  - Added CI perf job that runs the critical kernel on A100/GPU and G5 equivalent infra; collects baseline vs head; Slack perf-alert if >5% regression.
- In progress:
  - Numeric repro for f32/f16 mismatch on seq=4096 (WIP test harness). Expect a repro test by EOD Thu.
  - Kernel selector: adding rule to avoid v2 for flagged models until numeric test passes.
- Next:
  - If repro confirmed, roll back to v1 for affected model-variants and publish a mitigation note. Also open follow-up to adjust reduction order in kernel.

KV Cache (Aisha)
- Done:
  - Implemented sharded-KV map with lock-free readers for local host topology. Reduced memcopy hotspots in multi-tenant stress run.
  - Basic eviction policy switch from LRU->LRFU for longer contexts; improved hit-rate by ~3% for real workloads.
- In progress:
  - Prefetcher prototype to warm shards for rolling requests (tests show ~15% reduction in cold misses for steady-state workloads).
  - Instrumentation: added more KV metrics (shard_hit_ratio, shard_load, memcopy_bytes, prefetched_keys). Dashboard in Console-ops coming tomorrow.
- Risks / TODOs:
  - Prefetcher needs heuristics per-customer (some customers have synthetic traffic that confuses prefetch). Plan: add customer sampling and blacklist for noisy patterns.
  - Memory accounting for on-host multi-tenant cache not finalized; need SRE input for quota enforcement (ticket SERVRT-359).

Batching (Chen)
- Done:
  - Deployed alpha adaptive continuous batching to staging for routes: /v1/generate, /v1/chat. Initial metric window shows 7% token-cost reduction.
  - Added route-level config: max_batch_ms, max_batch_tokens, preferred_latency_slo.
- In progress:
  - Logic to handle short bursts: implementing predicted-arrival-rate smoothing to avoid oversized batches. Expect rollout to canary next week.
  - Better priority inversion handling when low-latency routes co-exist with throughput routes.
- Next:
  - Evaluate end-to-end with KV prefetcher enabled (Aisha) to measure combined effect on p99.

Standup notes (this week)
- Mon 08-10: Kernel CI flakiness observed on g5 cluster; Ben and Diego tracked to a container driver mismatch. Workaround pinned driver in CI.
- Tue 08-11: KV sharding demo to infra - showed memcopy reductions. Infra requested stronger SLOs for memory eviction.
- Wed 08-12: Batching canary rolled to 10% traffic for staging; two routes saw p50 spike, rolled back for those routes.

Action items (who / due)
- Ben: finish numeric repro + add unit test for fused-attn v2 (due 2026-08-14).
- Aisha: finalize prefetcher heuristics and start canary (due 2026-08-19).
- Chen: implement burst-smoothing in adaptive batching and test on canary (due 2026-08-18).
- Diego (SRE): propose memory quota eviction strategy for shard-backed KV caches (due 2026-08-17).
- Evelyn (Release eng): schedule a rollback window and communication plan if kernel v2 needs roll-back (due 2026-08-15).

Notes / loose thoughts:
- Consider exposing a "low_latency" route flag that disables adaptive batching entirely and forces strict size limits. Product asks for a simple toggle for customers.
- Long-term: investigate cross-host KV cache shared-memory layer to reduce memcopy for very large models. High complexity but big win for Dedicated.

Links & refs:
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1987
- Design: confluence.redwood.ai/display/SR/KV+Cache+Design
- Tickets: SERVRT-342 (kernel numeric), SERVRT-359 (kv memory accounting)

Meeting: Deep-dive (Wed 2026-08-12 10:30) attendees: Ben, Aisha, Chen, Diego, Evelyn
- Agenda: kernel regression triage, KV prefetch heuristics, batching burst smoothing plan
- Decisions: Add runbook steps for immediate rollback; prioritize kernel unit test; KV memory quota to be drafted by SRE this week.

Quick logs (raw / shorthand)
- ben: fused v2 landed, CI perf job green on a100 but failing on g5 -> pinned driver in CI
- aisha: sharded kv landed, prefetcher good but noisy customers -> add sampling
- chen: batching alpha canary -> 10% staging, two routes rolled back, smoothing logic next
- diego: container driver mismatch, looking at infra consistency; will propose driver matrix next

Document status: draft notes from weekly sync. Will update after kernel repro and SRE memory proposal.
summary: Weekly serving-runtime update covering kernel fused-attention v2, sharded KV cache prototype, and alpha adaptive batching. Key action items assigned; kernel numeric repro and KV memory quota are highest-priority blockers.
